title: It Must Be the Neighbours

pre.en: Where was the noise really coming from?
pre.zh: 噪音到底是从哪儿来的？
options: A building site near Chen's flat

intro: 一个视频会议上的小风波：会开到一半，忽然响起刺耳的噪音，大家各猜各的。读的时候留意人们怎么凭耳朵和眼睛下判断：It sounds like …、It looks as if …、It seems that …；再和 must、might、can't 的推测比一比，看谁的把握更大。

sentences.en: Every Tuesday, Rachel's team has a video call: Rachel in London, Arjun in Bangalore and Chen at home.
sentences.zh: 每周二，Rachel 的团队都要开视频会：Rachel 在伦敦，Arjun 在班加罗尔，小陈在家。

sentences.en: Last Tuesday, in the middle of the call, a nasty noise started.
sentences.zh: 上周二，会开到一半，响起了一阵刺耳的噪音。

sentences.en: It sounded as if someone was drilling through a wall.
sentences.zh: 听起来像有人在墙上钻孔。

sentences.en: And nobody could figure out where it was coming from.
sentences.zh: 可谁也搞不清声音是从哪儿来的。

sentences.en: "It sounds like a building site," said Arjun.
"Chen, didn't you say your neighbours were redecorating?"
sentences.zh: 「小陈，你不是说你家邻居在装修吗？」

sentences.en: "It must be them."
"I'm afraid not," said Chen.
"They finished last week."
"Well, it can't be me," said Rachel.
"I'm on mute."
On top of the noise, Arjun's audio kept cutting out.
sentences.zh: 除了噪音，Arjun 的声音还一直断断续续。

sentences.en: He'd run into this problem before.
sentences.zh: 他以前就碰到过这种问题。

sentences.en: Then it looked as if his screen had frozen, and for a moment the call went quiet.
sentences.zh: 接着他的画面看起来像是卡住了，通话一时安静了下来。

sentences.en: "Hold on," said Chen, and he headed for the window.
sentences.zh: 「等一下，」小陈说着，走到了窗边。

sentences.en: There was no building site outside.
So who, or what, was to blame?
sentences.zh: 那到底该怪谁，或者说该怪什么？

sentences.en: Then Chen pointed out something strange.
sentences.zh: 这时，小陈指出了一个奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: "The thing is, the noise stops whenever Rachel speaks."
sentences.zh: 「问题是，Rachel 一说话，噪音就停。」

sentences.en: "And it starts again when she's quiet."
"So it seems that it's coming from London."
sentences.zh: 「所以看来声音是从伦敦传来的。」

sentences.en: Rachel said nothing, and everyone listened in silence.
sentences.zh: Rachel 没出声，大家都静静地竖起耳朵听。

sentences.en: Boom, boom, crash.
"It sounds like drums," said Arjun.
"Rachel, you can't have been on mute at all!"
Rachel went red.
"That... might be my son," she said.
"He's learning the drums."
There was a short pause.
"By the way, he's very talented."

cards.note: during something, or at the centre of a place
名词 a drill 是电钻；drill a hole 钻个孔。
to understand or solve something after thinking about it
cards.tip: 代词放中间：figure it out，不说 figure out it。
cards.example: I finally figured out how to fix the layout.

cards.note: used to say what you think something is, from what you hear
cards.tip: like 后面接名词，口语里也常接句子：It sounds like you're busy. 听别人讲完一件事也能用：That sounds like fun!
cards.example: It sounds like the meeting went well.

cards.note: 英式说法，美式多说 construction site。
多指刷墙、换墙纸这类室内装修；大改造用 renovate。

cards.zh: 恐怕；（客气地说出坏消息）
cards.note: used to politely say something that the other person may not want to hear
if you are on mute in a call, other people cannot hear you
cards.tip: 开静音是 mute yourself / go on mute，取消静音是 unmute。开会时最常听到的一句：You're on mute!（你没开麦！）
cards.example: Sorry, I was on mute — can you hear me now?

cards.note: in addition to something, especially something difficult
视频会议里 audio 指声音，video 指画面：Your audio is fine, but your video is frozen.

cards.zh: （声音、信号）断断续续；突然中断
cards.note: if a sound or a machine cuts out, it suddenly stops working for a short time
cards.tip: 主语是声音、信号或人都行：You're cutting out.（你那边断断续续的。）kept cutting out 是「老是断」。
cards.example: Sorry, you're cutting out — could you say that again?

cards.note: to experience a problem or difficulty, often one you did not expect
cards.tip: 过去分词是 run（had run into），过去式是 ran；run into sb 是「碰巧遇见某人」。
cards.example: If you run into any problems, just message me.

cards.note: freeze 的过去分词；电脑、画面卡死都能说 freeze：My laptop froze.
to become silent
cards.tip: go 在这里是「变得」，后面接形容词；同类说法还有 go red（脸红）、go wrong（出错）。
cards.example: The room went quiet when the CEO walked in.

cards.note: used to ask someone to wait for a short time
cards.tip: 口语里比 wait 客气；打电话常说 Hold on a second / Hold on a minute。
cards.example: Hold on — I just need to find the link.

cards.note: to go towards a place
to be responsible for something bad that has happened
to tell someone something they did not know or had not noticed
cards.tip: 指出的东西放后面：point out a mistake；是代词就放中间：point it out。
cards.example: She pointed out a small mistake in my code.

cards.note: used to introduce a reason or a problem
used to add something, often on a different subject
cards.tip: 用来顺带提一件事或转换话题，常放句首；anyway 是把话题拉回来，方向正好相反。
cards.example: By the way, the client moved our call to Thursday.

cards.note: 名词是 talent：She has a real talent for design.
